item.title: Re: The Drag Strip Phantom / The Black Magnum [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
2) If you are going to make this the first, then you may want to include a way for it to be neutralized, and not just temporarily. Also, no fear of death is likely to create an SCP that is going to be a lot rougher and therefore be harder to contain. The GOI in question may have actually been in the right.

If there does seem to be more of these, then it's possible that The Foundation may assign an MTF or two if they become a major problem.

3) If the phantom simply possesses another car then there is no reason for the memories to carry over; it's the same entity so it would have the same memories. If the phantom died or there was some sort of hive mentality I could see a reason for the note, but since it's not a reincarnation, a new phantom. or otherwise a new entity there's no reason for the note.

item.title: Re: The Drag Strip Phantom / The Black Magnum [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
1)Yeah, that is true. I'll render only communication between dimensions impossible.

2)The Camaro is only the first, more manifestations will crop up later on. Also, no, the phantoms don't fear death - they don't remember its concept from their past lives. Why do you bring it up?

3)The phantoms' memories carry over from one vessel to another - it's established when the Foundation sends a copy of the GoI car to the Camaro - it is then attacked by the SCP.

4)You have a point. I'll change that part so that phantoms can manifest as undead but have very crude comunication skills and are tethered to their cars.

5)A lot of this is concepts and worldbuilding just to help me understand what this SCP is in the first place so it behaves logically. I'll definitely describe it much less in the Foundation's article.

Thanks for the review!

item.title: Re: The Drag Strip Phantom / The Black Magnum [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
First, some necessary simplifications:
1) If the dimension effectively disables electronics then that makes exploring the dimension harder. While this makes uncovering its mysteries, this falls under the "too many anomalies" header, and that eliminates part of the fun. Basically, you've got a mysterious car, you have a cool dimension, that should be enough.

2) If this car is constantly challenging other cars and anyone that dies on the strip becomes another manifestation, then why do we only see the one manifestation? There should be a lot of these vehicles running around. Also, if the phantom can merely possess another vehicle when it dies then it has no fear of death.

3) Also, how do you mean "memory beyond its current vessel"? Also, how was it established?

4) You can't have the phantom as a "mysterious force" and not know if there's a driver if the force can possess others and modify vehicles. That eliminates the question one way or the other.

5) Basically, you have a lot of interesting things here, and you may have too many of them. Focus on the ones that are important to the SCP and eliminate the rest.

item.title: The Drag Strip Phantoms
item.content:encoded:
An SCP heavily and very directly inspired by Christine, The Wraith, Death Proof and SLR:Redline.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery/Thriller

Page Layout (Optional): Standard description and event chronology as well as mission reports and test logs

Elevator Pitch: The phantom of a car that manifests itself on lonely stretches of desert road at night to challenge high-performance passer-by cars to a drag race. Original manifestation is 1970 Camaro, however the list will expand later.

Central Narrative: A rumor spreads in a small town in Colorado about a mysterious "ghost car", originating from a local drag racing enthusiast. According to the legend, the racer is overtaken by a dragster and the road eventually leads into a foggy, abandoned drag strip - with a stoplight and everything. The Foundation takes note after several others report the same occurence and dispatches a team to study the anomaly up-close and personal ("prodding" the car during manifestations and exploring the strip dimension), as well as launching an investigation into the car's possible origins.

+ show block
– hide block

At one point, a GoI destroys it with a rocket launcher. A week later the phantom manifests in the closest town and has a brief run-in with a used car salesman while stealing a new muscle car. The Foundation attempts to contain the phantom following its rediscovery, as well as manage new cases of the SCP cropping up. In addition, the original phantom has now gained an apparent interest in humans.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The mystery surrounding the car itself: Is it sentient, is it dangerous, what is the drag strip, is/was it a real place, where does the car come from, is there anyone driving it, what is its driving force etc. etc. Later on, the phantoms' interactions with humans.

Additional Notes: The drag strip is a separate dimension that renders back-and-forth communication impossible./Cars cannot leave the dimension unless they engage in the race or get totaled./Anyone who dies on the strip in a car becomes another manifestation./The phantoms are free to switch or modify their vessels./Phantoms all have a physical form as their previous selves' corpses./If a phantom's manifestation is "killed", a new one will appear after some time, depending on the damage./Each phantom is sentient and remembers its entire "afterlife"./Phantoms have little to no memory of their past lives./The SCP can manifest at will anytime between sunset and dawn./It is not bound to any road in particular and can move at any time.

P.S. Apologies to everyone who got my email with no subject, I was very concentrated on getting outreach first
P.P.S. Apologies for the title being somewhat inconsistent with the idea, I posted this on accident when I wasn't done yet and constantly reedited it.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
